faq: Can you extend the core WooCommerce REST API?
Yes. We can add fields to existing orders and products, or add new routes in your own namespace. We choose the approach that keeps your changes safe through WooCommerce updates.
How do you secure the endpoints?
Every route has authentication, a permission check and strict input validation. We support WooCommerce API keys or application passwords, and never expose customer data without a capability check.
Do you build the system on the other end too?
We connect to it. If the other system has an API, send its documentation and we confirm the fit. Building the other system itself is a separate piece of work.
No. We queue deliveries with Action Scheduler, so the customer's checkout finishes first and the call goes out in the background. Failed deliveries are retried and logged.
desc:
WooCommerce REST API and webhooks work connects your plugin with CRMs, ERPs, shipping tools and your own apps. Ecom Swift LLC builds secured custom endpoints and outgoing webhooks, validates every request and documents each call with examples.

## What are WooCommerce REST API endpoints and webhooks?

A REST API endpoint is a web address that other software can call to read or change data. A webhook works in the other direction: your store sends a message to another system when something happens, such as a new order or a customer update.

WooCommerce already ships with a REST API for products, orders and customers. Custom endpoints add what that API does not cover, such as data stored by your plugin, special actions or a simpler format for another system.

## Why do custom endpoints need careful design?

An endpoint is a door into your store. If it lacks authentication, anyone can call it. If it skips permission checks, a user with a low role can read or change data meant only for administrators. If it does not validate input, bad data can corrupt records or trigger errors.

Poorly designed endpoints are also hard to use. Other developers need clear field names, consistent responses and meaningful errors. Without them, every integration turns into guesswork and support requests.

## How a clean API layer supports growth

Once a plugin exposes a stable API, other tools can connect without changes to your core code. A warehouse system can read orders, a mobile app can show customer data and a partner can build on your plugin.

Webhooks reduce load as well. Instead of another system asking your store for updates every few minutes, your store tells it once, when something changes. That uses less server time and delivers news sooner.

## What a well-built API and webhook setup includes

- Endpoints registered with the WordPress REST API, using clear namespaces and versions.
- Authentication, plus permission checks on every route.
- Input validation and sanitizing for each parameter.
- Clear error messages and sensible status codes.
- Outgoing webhooks for orders, customers or your own events.
- Retry on failed delivery and a log of each attempt.
- Signed webhook payloads, so the receiver can confirm the sender.
- Paging and rate limits for endpoints that return lists.
- Example requests, a Postman collection and an API reference.
- A test suite that checks each endpoint.

## What we do

We begin by mapping the data flow: which system asks for what, which events must be pushed out and who is allowed to call each endpoint. We write this as a short interface specification for your approval.

We then build the routes and webhooks on a staging copy, test them with real requests and check failure cases such as missing fields, wrong permissions and a receiver that is offline. To keep checkout fast, webhooks are sent in the background and not while the customer waits. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in the number of endpoints and webhook topics, and in whether logs, retries, signed payloads, paging and a test suite are included.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Decide who needs access and give each client only what it needs.
- Use separate keys for separate systems.
- Version your endpoints so later changes do not break old clients.
- Verify webhook signatures on the receiving side.
- Keep the example requests next to your documentation.

**Avoid:**
- Opening an endpoint to the public when it handles customer data.
- Returning more fields than the client needs.
- Sending webhooks from the checkout request itself.
- Sharing secret keys in emails or chat.
- Changing response formats without warning.

## Who this service is for

This service suits a plugin author who needs a mobile app or partner tool to read data from the plugin. It suits a store that must push new orders into an ERP or fulfillment system. It also suits an agency building a headless front end that needs a few custom routes beside the standard WooCommerce API.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of the systems involved, the data each one needs and the events that should trigger a webhook. If the other system has its own API documentation, include it. We build the WooCommerce side only, unless agreed otherwise. We never ask for passwords. Access is given as a developer or collaborator user, or through a staging site.
